algorithm: Alternating-path BFS; one attempt per active unmatched root, visited rows/holes per attempt, reverse augmenting path on free hole, exhausted reached-row Hall cut on failure. No matching/subset/SAT assignment enumeration.
mandatory_validation: Every returned certificate passes an explicit if-not validator check that raises RuntimeError on failure, including under Python -O. Invalid graph input raises TypeError/ValueError; it is never returned as a failure certificate.
checked_theorem: Inverse-consistent row/owner tables and unmatched root with full-neighborhood owner closure imply strict Hall deficiency
If all reached rows are active, existing failureCheck accepts the derived cut
Such an exhausted search state excludes matching
precise_theorem_premises: every hole in the FULL neighbor union of S has an owner inside S
every row in S is active for validator acceptance
missing_inductions: Initial partial matching, neighbor validity, active domain and inverse-table consistency
BFS parent-chain and discovery invariants, active reached rows, and no repeated enqueues
Augmenting path reconstruction preserves neighbor validity/injection/both matching tables and increases matched-row count by one
Queue exhaustion yields full-neighborhood owner closure with no free hole and unmatched root
Completion of outer active-root loop yields accepted success certificate
operation_counts: Instrumented graph operations satisfy at most a attempts, a*a row expansions, a*m active-edge scans, and a*a path updates on completed runs (a active rows, m active edges). This is not a formal encoded-bit bound.
next_research_target: Formalize augmentation and BFS invariant preservation for a typed executable search, then apply the checked exhausted-cut implication at failure and accepted-success theorem at completion. Keep the existing certifying constructor boundary for outputs.
counting_scope: Do not count this as a fully verified matching-search component. The kernel-checked addition is the failed-search implication under explicit invariants; implementation tests and finite cross-language certificates are separate evidence.
